title: Align prompt-too-long retry grouping for compact summary
objective: Replace Go's coarse oldest-turn PTL retry strategy with TS-style API-round truncation that preserves valid provider boundaries.
implementation_scope: Implement truncateHeadForPTLRetry using API-round groups rather than findNextTurnEnd.
When truncation would produce assistant-first messages, prepend a synthetic user marker equivalent to the TS PTL retry marker.
Thread truncated messages through both structured and fallback summary paths.
Emit explicit compact PTL retry events or debug logs with attempt, dropped message count, and remaining message count.
Stop after the TS-equivalent maximum retry count and return a typed prompt-too-long compact error.
out_of_scope: Do not implement reactive compact in this task.
Do not change the general query loop retry policy.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover assistant-fragment API rounds, single human turn with many tool loops, assistant-first retry slices, and retry exhaustion.
PTL retry never reintroduces stripped images or unbudgeted oversized tool results.
Summary compaction fallback to HistorySnip is not used for ordinary recoverable compact PTL before retries are exhausted.
risks: API-round grouping depends on assistant ids; if unavailable for some provider paths, define a conservative fallback and test it.
dispatch_prompt: Implement TS-equivalent compact prompt-too-long retry grouping in Go, using API-round groups and synthetic user markers for assistant-first slices.
